name: Kool G Rap
hook: A Corona, Queens rapper whose dense, multisyllabic crime narratives on 'Road to the Riches' (1989) are widely credited with starting mafioso rap.

blurb.age7: Kool G Rap was a rapper known for very complicated, fast rhymes about crime stories. Lots of later rappers copied his style.
blurb.age13: Nathaniel Wilson, born in 1968, grew up in Corona, Queens, and connected with DJ Polo and producer Marley Marl through the Juice Crew. As Kool G Rap and DJ Polo, their 1989 album 'Road to the Riches', produced entirely by Marl, paired dense, multisyllabic rhyme patterns with crime and gangster storytelling years before that combination became its own subgenre, mafioso rap.
blurb.adult: 'Road to the Riches' (1989) is widely cited as mafioso rap's founding document, years ahead of the subgenre's better-known 1990s wave. Kool G Rap's technical rhyme density, internal rhymes and multisyllabic patterns packed into a single bar, is one of the most directly cited influences on the more elaborate lyrical styles that followed him in the 1990s.
